title: What FDI does to the host economy

predict.q: Foreign firms build several new factories in a developing country. On an AD/AS diagram, what happens?

options.s: AD shifts right now, and LRAS shifts right as the factories start producing
options.fb: Building the factories is investment spending (AD now); once running, they add capacity (LRAS later), so the price rise fades.

options.s: Only AD shifts right: the price level rises, with no change in capacity
options.fb: The factories add capacity once running, so LRAS shifts too; the price rise is temporary.

options.s: LRAS shifts left, because profits will flow out of the country
options.fb: Profit outflows reduce GNI, not the economy's capacity to produce; the new plants raise capacity.

options.s: Nothing changes, because the spending is done by foreign firms
options.fb: Investment spending on factories inside the country is part of its AD, whoever pays for it.

task: Move the **inward FDI** slider, then switch from **short run** to **long run**, and watch both curves.

target.do: Move the FDI slider up, then switch to long run, then press Check.

takeaway: FDI is **investment** spending now (AD) and **extra productive capacity** later (LRAS), so output can grow with less inflation.
